note: Trial plan: each picture has a second idea in "candidates" to choose between by eye.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye.

sections.meaning: All people spoke one language, and they journeyed east together until they found a plain in Shinar and settled there.
ideas: A big crowd of every age on an open plain, all singing one song with one voice
Neighbors laughing and talking easily over a low brick garden wall
A long line of travelers on foot with bundles coming down a hillside onto a vast plain
Aerial view of two slow rivers across a wide fertile plain with a small camp of tents arriving
Two strangers meeting on a road and greeting each other in the very same words
A class of children answering a teacher together in one voice
A single wide river valley seen from a hill pass at midday with a thin line of walkers
A town square where everyone is clapping the same rhythm
A signal flag raised and a whole crowd turning as one
A family wagon crossing a plain with a long trail of dust behind

sections.meaning: They made hard-fired brick and tar their stone and mortar, and set out to build a city and a tower reaching the sky to make a name for themselves.
ideas: A bricklayer's hands pressing a kiln-fired brick into black tar on a rising wall
A brickyard of tidy stacks of red bricks beside a glowing kiln, no people
A colossal red-brick tower wrapped in scaffolding with its top lost in cloud above a new brick city

A line of workers carrying bricks up long ladders

sections.meaning: Yahweh comes down to look at what they have built, sees one people with one speech and nothing out of their reach, and decides to confuse their speech so that they cannot understand each other.
ideas: Seen from above through a wide break in the cloud, the unfinished tower and its city far below
A single shaft of light falling from a break in dark cloud onto the unfinished tower

A tangle of cables each plugged into the wrong socket
Raindrops of different sizes falling on a single lake

sections.meaning: Work stops on the city, and from there Yahweh scatters the people over the whole earth, so the place is named for the confusion.
ideas: The unfinished tower silent and abandoned, tools and wheelbarrows left where they were dropped

A cracked clay jug whose pieces lie scattered over a floor
